assets.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational.
Asset type: 12-panel cumulative raster drawing tutorial, EXACTLY 4 equal columns by 3 equal rows, landscape 2048x1536. Each panel will be individually cropped by a beginner drawing app.
Input image is the design reference of the lion boss; preserve that golden angular mane, black mechanical mane spikes with cyan inset lights, feline closed muzzle and proud narrowed golden eye. This is a true RIGHT-FACING PROFILE head-and-shoulders portrait, one visible eye, muzzle points RIGHT; back of mane LEFT. Keep identical head position, size and profile in all 12 panels. No perspective or pose change.
A careful gradual sketch-to-ink tutorial ordered left-to-right then next row:
1 only a light simple circle for the skull and a short curved neck, plenty of room around it for mane.
2 add a short broad muzzle block projecting right and rounded jaw below.
3 refine small feline nose and closed mouth.
4 add one narrowed eye and brow.
5 add one small round ear nestled behind eye.
6 add big rough pale outline of the entire mane around back and down chest.
7 divide mane silhouette into 7 large irregular pointed fur groups.
8 add inner grouped fur around cheek, chin and chest.
9 add several black mechanical blade outlines following the back-of-mane contour; no color yet.
10 add small inset indicator shapes and mechanical joins on mane blades.
11 trace clean dark ink contour with short varied feathered fur marks; erase pale construction.
12 complete clean UNCOLORED ink line art of the profile head, with sparse black ink masses in mechanical plates and deep mane overlaps.
Only the head, full mane, neckline and a tiny upper-collar hint, NOT entire body. Uncolored graphite-to-black ink raster artwork, warm white paper, thin faint neutral grid. Each cell same scale and margins, no crop, no panel-to-panel drift. Avoid text, numbers, labels, arrows, color fills. No wolf: round lion ears, broad feline muzzle and massive mane. No weapon, no attack. This is actual drawn art with subtle lively ink line, not vector primitives or stick diagram.

Use case: scientific-educational.
Asset type: cumulative beginner raster character drawing contact sheet, EXACTLY FOUR COLUMNS and THREE ROWS of equal cells, 2048x1536 landscape. No text or numbers.

Near-side right mechanical arm hangs in front of his side with hand lowered, far arm tucked calmly behind back. He wears fitted black and crimson long tailcoat with high collar, cream waistcoat, dark trousers, tall multi-strapped boots. Long tail curves to LEFT with dark tuft. Slender rapier held loosely DOWNWARD diagonal toward lower RIGHT, nonattacking idle pose.

Every cell shows the WHOLE same standing body area, with complete head and increasingly completed body; maintain identical position and scale, head near upper left-of-center, boot soles same baseline, enough margins for lowered sword. All lineart, no color, no gray shading except very faint construction. Row-major cumulative stages:
1 completed profile head and mane above a light simple torso-and-pelvis construction and one faint ground line; NO limbs yet.
2 add simple two leg cylinders and wedge feet standing naturally.
3 add fitted waistcoat outline and lapel folds on torso.
4 add long tailcoat silhouette with split tails extending behind LEFT.
5 add large lapels, high collar and coat seams.
6 add near mechanical arm upper arm/forearm block shapes hanging down, no hand details yet.
7 add articulated mechanical elbow, armor plates and hanging gripping mechanical hand.
8 add far organic arm bent behind back, sleeve and cuff.
9 refine trousers and both tall boot silhouettes over the leg construction.
10 add boot straps/buckles, waist belt and short hip chain.
11 add long curved lion tail and tuft behind LEFT, and the relaxed rapier guard in hand with long thin blade pointing down RIGHT. Blade must fit panel boundaries.
12 clean whole full-body black ink drawing, erase light construction, refine grouped mane and ragged coat edges.
Do not add new objects, change pose, change clothing, render extra eyes or make the lion a wolf. No movement or attack. Fine handdrawn concept art, clean white warm paper, thin pale grid separators, no border decorations, no captions, no panel digits, no watermark. Each panel is a useful real drawing demonstration, not a geometric diagram.
CRITICAL ADDITION: Image 2 is an APPROVED SIDE-PROFILE COLORING SHEET. Match its lion's final panel body silhouette EXACTLY, including narrow SIDE-VIEW torso and legs visually overlapping, ONE dominant boot silhouette pointing right, opposite leg barely visible behind. Image 1 supplies original design details only. Do NOT use a front-facing chest, splayed knees or broad frontal pelvis. DO NOT copy the grid image itself as tiny subpanels: produce the requested twelve full-size sequential construction cells.
The body in every panel must correspond directly to image 2 final pose, so the end of this lesson can lead into that coloring sheet seamlessly. Center the whole standing lion slightly LEFT within each cell, shrink the whole figure enough to leave 7% margin under boots and under sword tip, 7% margin to the right of rapier tip, 7% to left of tail. All sword and tail pixels MUST fit inside each cell without touching borders. Final sword points toward bottom-right at roughly 45 degrees, not horizontal. The long coat trails behind LEFT. Far arm is calmly behind his back. The right arm is the visible near-side mechanical arm.
